40021941.author: पदार्थः
40021941.content: एषः this, ते to you, नृगशापस्य of Nṛga's curse, विस्तरः the detailed account, अभिहितः has been told, मया by me, यदि if, अस्ति there is, श्रवणे in listening, श्रद्धा faith/desire, शृणुष्व listen, इह here, अपराम् another, कथाम् story.

40021941.author: Translation
40021941.content: I have told you this detailed account of Nṛga's curse; if you have a desire to listen, then hear another story here.

40021942.author: पदार्थः
40021942.content: एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तु but, रामेण by Rama, सौमित्रिः Saumitri (Lakshmana), पुनः again, अब्रवीत् spoke, तृप्तिः satisfaction, आश्चर्यभूतानाम् of wonderful, कथानाम् stories, न not, अस्ति is, मे to me, नृप O king.

40021942.author: Translation
40021942.content: But thus spoken to by Rama, Saumitri spoke again, saying, "O king, I have no satisfaction from wonderful stories."

40021943.author: पदार्थः
40021943.content: लक्ष्मणेन by Lakshmana, एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तु but, रामः Rama, इक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः the delight of the Ikshvakus, कथाम् a story, परमधर्मिष्ठाम् most righteous, व्याहर्तुम् to narrate, उपचक्रमे began.

40021943.author: Translation
40021943.content: But thus spoken to by Lakshmana, Rama, the delight of the Ikshvakus, began to narrate a most righteous story.

40021944.author: पदार्थः
40021944.content: आसीत् was, राजा a king, निमिः Nimi, नाम by name, इक्ष्वाकूणाम् among the Ikshvakus, महात्मनाम् of great souls, पुत्रः son, द्वादशमः twelfth, वीर्ये in valor, धर्मे in righteousness, च and, परिनिष्ठितः firmly established

40021944.author: Translation
40021944.content: There was a king named Nimi, the twelfth son among the noble Ikshvakus, who was firmly established in both valor and righteousness.

40021945.author: पदार्थः
40021945.content: सः that, राजा king, वीर्यसम्पन्नः endowed with valor, पुरम् a city, देवपुरोपमम् resembling a city of gods, निवेशयामास established, तदा then, अभ्याशे near, गौतमस्य of Gautama, तु indeed

40021945.author: Translation
40021945.content: That valiant king then founded a city, resembling a divine city, near the hermitage of Gautama.

40021946.author: पदार्थः
40021946.content: पुरस्य of the city, सुकृतम् well-made, नाम by name, वैजयन्तम् Vaijayanta, इति thus, श्रुतम् known, निवेशम् settlement, यत्र where, राजर्षिः the royal sage, निमिः Nimi, चक्रे made, महायशाः greatly renowned

40021946.author: Translation
40021946.content: The city was known as Sukrita, or Vaijayanta, where the greatly renowned royal sage Nimi established his settlement.

40021947.author: पदार्थः
40021947.content: तस्य to him, बुद्धिः thought, समुत्पन्ना arose, निवेश्य having established, सुमहापुरम् a very great city, यजेयम् I should sacrifice, दीर्घसत्रेण with a long sacrifice, पितुः of the father, प्रह्लादयन् delighting, मनः the mind

40021947.author: Translation
40021947.content: After establishing that magnificent city, the thought arose in him, "I should perform a long sacrifice, delighting my father's mind."

40021948.author: पदार्थः
40021948.content: ततः thereafter, पितरम् father, आमन्त्र्य having invited, इक्ष्वाकुम् Ikshvaku, हि indeed, मनोः of Manu, सुतम् the son, वसिष्ठम् Vasishtha, वरयामास chose, पूर्वम् first, ब्रह्मर्षिसत्तमम् the foremost among Brahmarishis

40021948.author: Translation
40021948.content: Thereafter, having consulted his father Ikshvaku, the son of Manu, he first chose Vasishtha, the foremost among Brahmarishis, to officiate the sacrifice.

40021949.author: पदार्थः
40021949.content: अनन्तरम् thereafter, स that, राजर्षिः royal sage, निमिः Nimi, इक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः descendant of Ikshvaku, अत्रिम् Atri, अङ्गिरसम् Angiras, च एव and also, भृगुम् Bhrigu, च एव and also, तपोधनम् rich in penance,

40021949.author: Translation
40021949.content: Subsequently, the royal sage Nimi, a descendant of Ikshvaku, approached Atri, Angiras, and Bhrigu, who were rich in penance.

40021950.author: पदार्थः
40021950.content: तम् to him, उवाच said, वसिष्ठः Vasishtha, तु however, निमिम् to Nimi, राजर्षिसत्तमम् the best among royal sages, वृतः chosen, अहम् I am, पूर्वम् previously, इन्द्रेण by Indra, अन्तरम् an interval, प्रतिपालय wait for,

40021950.author: Translation
40021950.content: However, Vasishtha said to Nimi, the best of royal sages, "I have already been chosen by Indra, so please wait for some time."

40021951.author: पदार्थः
40021951.content: अनन्तरम् thereafter, महाविप्रः the great brahmin, गौतमः Gautama, प्रत्यपूरयत् fulfilled (the request), वसिष्ठः Vasishtha, अपि also, महातेजा greatly effulgent, इन्द्रयज्ञम् Indra's sacrifice, अथ then, अकरोत् performed,

40021951.author: Translation
40021951.content: Subsequently, the great brahmin Gautama fulfilled Nimi's request, while the greatly effulgent Vasishtha then performed Indra's sacrifice.

40021952.author: पदार्थः
40021952.content: निमिः Nimi, तु however, राजा king, विप्रान् those brahmins, तान् them, समानीय having gathered, नराधिपः the lord of men, अयजत् performed sacrifice, हिमवत्पार्श्वे on the side of the Himalayas, स्वपुरस्य of his own city, समीपतः near, पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि for five thousand years, राजा the king, दीक्षाम् the vow (of sacrifice), उपागमत् undertook,

40021952.author: Translation
40021952.content: King Nimi, the lord of men, however, gathered those brahmins and performed a sacrifice near his own city, on the side of the Himalayas, undertaking the sacrificial vow for five thousand years.

40021953.author: पदार्थः
40021953.content: इन्द्रयज्ञावसाने at the conclusion of Indra's sacrifice, तु however, वसिष्ठः Vasishtha, भगवन् divine, ऋषिः sage, सकाशम् near, आगतः came, राज्ञः of the king, हौत्रम् the role of hotri, कर्तुम् to perform, अनिन्दितः blameless,

40021953.author: Translation
40021953.content: However, at the conclusion of Indra's sacrifice, the blameless divine sage Vasishtha came near the king to perform the role of the hotri priest.

40021954.author: पदार्थः
40021954.content: तदन्तरम् thereafter, अथ then, अपश्यत् (he) saw, गौतमेन by Gautama, अभिपूरितम् filled (the place), कोपेन with anger, महता great, आविष्टः overcome, वसिष्ठः Vasiṣṭha, ब्रह्मणः of Brahma, सुतः the son.

40021954.author: Translation
40021954.content: Then, Vasiṣṭha, the son of Brahma, saw the place occupied by Gautama and was overcome with great anger.

40021955.author: पदार्थः
40021955.content: सः He, राज्ञः of the king, दर्शनाकाङ्क्षी desirous of seeing, मुहूर्तम् for a moment, समुपाविशत् sat down, तस्मिन् on that, अहनि day, राजर्षिः the royal sage, निद्रया by sleep, अपहृतः overcome, भृशम् greatly.

40021955.author: Translation
40021955.content: Desirous of seeing the king, Vasiṣṭha sat down for a moment, but on that day, the royal sage was deeply overcome by sleep.

40021956.author: पदार्थः
40021956.content: ततः Then, मन्युः anger, वसिष्ठस्य of Vasiṣṭha, प्रादुरासीत् arose, महात्मनः of the great-souled one, अदर्शनेन by the non-seeing, राजर्षेः of the royal sage, व्याहर्तुम् to speak, उपचक्रमे began.

40021956.author: Translation
40021956.content: Then, anger arose in the great-souled Vasiṣṭha due to the absence of the royal sage, and he began to speak.

40021957.author: पदार्थः
40021957.content: यस्मात् because, त्वम् you, अन्यम् another, वृतवान् have chosen, माम् me, अवज्ञाय disregarding, पार्थिव O King, चेतनेन with consciousness, विनाभूतः devoid of, देहः body, तव your, भविष्यति will be.

40021957.author: Translation
40021957.content: "O King, because you have chosen another, disregarding me, your body will become devoid of consciousness."

40021958.author: पदार्थः
40021958.content: ततः Then, प्रबुद्धः awakened, राजर्षिः the royal sage, श्रुत्वा having heard, शापम् the curse, उदाहृतम् uttered, ब्रह्मयोनिम् to the one born from Brahma, अथ then, उवाच spoke, संरम्भात् from agitation, क्रोधमूर्च्छितः overcome with anger.

40021958.author: Translation
40021958.content: Then, the royal sage, awakened and having heard the uttered curse, spoke to Vasiṣṭha, the son of Brahma, overcome with fury and anger.

40021959.author: पदार्थः
40021959.content: अजानतः unaware, शयानस्य of one who was sleeping, क्रोधेन by anger, कलुषीकृतः enraged, मुक्तवान् he released, मयि upon me, शापाग्निं the fire of a curse, यमदण्डम् the rod of Yama, इव like, अपरम् another.

40021959.author: Translation
40021959.content: Enraged by anger, he, unaware of me sleeping, cast upon me the fire of a curse, like a second rod of Yama.

40021960.author: पदार्थः
40021960.content: तस्मात् therefore, तवापि even your, ब्रह्मर्षे O Brahmarshi, चेतनेन by consciousness, विना कृतः deprived of, देहः body, सुरुचिरप्रख्यो exceedingly charming in appearance, भविष्यति will be, न संशयः no doubt.

40021960.author: Translation
40021960.content: Therefore, O Brahmarshi, without a doubt, even your exceedingly charming body will be deprived of consciousness.

40021961.author: पदार्थः
40021961.content: इति thus, रोषवशात् due to the power of anger, उभौ both, तदानीम् then, अन्योन्यं each other, शपितौ cursed, नृपद्विजेन्द्रौ the king and the chief of Brahmins, सहसैव suddenly, बभूवतुः became, विदेहौ bodiless, तत्तुल्याधिगतप्रभाववन्तौ possessing equally acquired power.

40021961.author: Translation
40021961.content: Thus, under the sway of anger, both the king and the chief of Brahmins, having cursed each other, suddenly became bodiless, each possessing an equally acquired power. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 55 ।। Thus ends the fifty-fifth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
